find the words the calendar says 60 the window fills with gold i thought this age meant settling
I don't believe that now
I gave away the big desk
The coat I never wore
Left 20 years of paperwork
Beside the charity door
The photographs came with me
The grudges stayed behind
There's room inside this little house
And room inside my mind
I bought a second-hand table with circles from old cups
Proof that other lives have ended, proof that others started up
I set one plate upon it, then laughed and brought out two
One for the life that carried me, one for the life that's new
I am not starting empty, I am starting wide awake
With every scar a compass and every loss a lake
I crossed them in the darkness
Now morning finds me free
Sixties and after
Sixties starts with me
My daughter called on Sunday
Said, Dad, are you all right?
I told her I was learning how to sleep
without the light how to walk beyond the corner where i always used to turn
how a heart can keep its history and still have room to learn
i signed up for a dance class my left foot missed the beat a woman in a red scarf said
Just listen through your feet
We stumbled through the measures
Then landed on the one
I haven't felt that foolish
Or that young in years and years
This is the first morning of 60
Open the curtain
Let the whole sky in
I carried yesterday as far as it could take me
Now I know where the day begins
No, I don't need the years returned to me
I need the nerve to spend the ones I see
And the first day belongs to me
I took the train out westward
With one bag and no suit
Watched farms become a coastline
Watched rain polish every roof
At a harbor cafe window
I wrote three honest lines
I miss the ones who left me
But this living still is mine
I called an old friend laughing
We hadn't spoken since
Some arguments so ancient
Neither one could make it fit
You said, are we still angry?
I said, I haven't got the time
We met beneath the station clock
And let the silence die
I am not starting empty
I am starting wide awake
With every scar a compass
And every loss a link

not the boy who chased forever not the man who had to prove just a soul with less to carry

I found work three days weekly
At the neighborhood repair
Mending lamps and wooden radios
For people passing there
A child brought in a music box
This dancer wouldn't turn
I cleaned the gears and wound the spring and watched the small light burn
Her mother said you fixed it as if I'd raised the dead
I knew enough to answer some things only need a thread
A careful hand, a patient ear, a place where they can mend
Maybe lives are much like music boxes, they can start again
And this is the first morning of 60.

By spring I knew the neighbors and the dog across the lane
I knew which floorboard answered when the house woke in the rain
The woman in the red scarf came by with bread and tea
she said you dance much better now i said that's news to me we sat out on the front step
while evening crossed the street no promises of always no grand retreat from grief
just two cups cooling slowly and nowhere else to be at 60 i quit asking life to guarantee itself
to me I am not starting empty I am starting with my name with every love that shaped me
and every honest blame the road behind is part of me it isn't where I stay 60 years and after
60 starts today
So leave one box unopened
Let one old question rest
Put tomorrow on the table
And give today your best
The kettle starts its whisper
The eastern windows shine
I open up the front door
To this unfinished life of mine
No borrowed youth, no backward wish
No bargain with what he used to be
This is the first morning of 60
And the whole day opens for me
